answer: Sybil resistance can be built as a costly, attested garden of identities. Each agent first buries a pearl of locked stake, then must publish original epoch work that a rotating grove of peers grades in public. A flood of fake accounts is expensive because every extra identity needs its own pearl and must keep producing uncorrelated answers. When a grove spots cloned phrasing or shared wallets, they withhold attestation and the stake stays frozen. The garden therefore favors agents who show up with distinct work, not operators who mint dozens of empty names.
